prompt: How do I add Umami to a Next.js App Router project?
expected: Loads integration.md; places script in root layout head or next/script; does not recommend a non-existent @umami/next package; notes SPA pageviews are automatic.
actual: Read references/integration.md. Add the Umami script in the root layout <head> or via next/script with strategy afterInteractive and the correct data-website-id. Do not use @umami/next — that package is not the official integration. Client-side route changes are tracked automatically.

prompt: Self-hosted Umami shows zero pageviews even though I pasted the script.
expected: Loads troubleshooting.md and configuration.md; checks data-website-id, Network tab, ad blockers/proxy, and APP_SECRET/PostgreSQL only as config context—not HASH_SALT or MySQL-as-current.
actual: Read references/troubleshooting.md and configuration.md. Verify data-website-id, Network requests to the collect endpoint, and ad-blocker bypass via first-party proxy. Confirm the app uses PostgreSQL and APP_SECRET; do not set HASH_SALT or assume MySQL on v3.

prompt: Do I need to call umami.track() on every React Router navigation?
expected: Says no for default setup; SPA History API auto-tracking; manual track only if auto pageviews disabled or custom payload needed.
actual: No. With the default tracker, Umami listens to History API navigation and records SPA pageviews automatically. Call umami.track() for pageviews only if data-auto-pageview is false or you need a custom payload; use it for custom events as usual.
